documents: Wang, Zhou, Xing, Bao & Zhang (2022), Seasonal variation of long-chain alkyl diols proxies in suspended particulate matter of the Changjiang River Estuary, JGR Biogeosciences 127, e2022JG007049 (published PDF, 16 pages)
pages_convention: PDF pages counted from 1 (these match the printed 'n of 16' article pages); supplementary material not supplied

entry.evidence: few studies reported seasonal variation in LCDs and evaluated their applicability as environmental indicators in modern marine environments

steps.action: Posed the question of how seasonal variation affects LCD proxies (DI for salinity, LDI for SST, NDI/1,14-diols for nutrients, FC32 1,15-diol for riverine input) in a river-dominated estuary.
steps.quote: Thus, assessing the impact of seasonal variation on DI proxy indicating salinity remains critical.

steps.action: Took the four published proxy relationships as the claims to be evaluated: DI and salinity (Versteegh), LDI and SST (Rampen), 1,14-diols and nutrients (Gal), and FC32 1,15-diol and riverine input (Lattaud, de Bar).
steps.quote: correlated well with the annual average SST in different oceans (Rampen et al., 2012).

steps.action: Chose surface-water suspended particulate matter collected in different seasons as the target material, and the CRE salinity and nutrient gradient as the setting.
steps.quote: To study seasonal variation in LCDs proxies, suspended particulate matter (SPM) in surface seawater may be as an effective target material.

steps.action: Collected 36 SPM samples on NSFC open cruises in May 2017, July 2017 and March 2018, along a transect from the river to offshore, by filtering 100–200 L of water pumped from about 5 m depth.
steps.quote: Samples of SPM were collected in spring (May 2017; Figure 1b), summer (July 2017; Figure 1c), and winter (March 2018; Figure 1d)

steps.action: Extracted, fractionated and derivatized the lipids, then measured the LCDs by GC-MS/MS in SIM mode, and the alkenones and sterols by GC-FID.
steps.quote: The LCDs were analyzed using an Agilent 7890A-G70001B gas chromatography-mass spectrometry system

steps.action: Checked the analysis with procedural blanks and with parallel measurements of samples (RSD <5%).
steps.quote: Sample blanks were measured and no target compounds were detected.

steps.action: Reported the six LCDs and their relative abundances by season and zone (river, estuary and offshore, with salinity boundaries of 5 and 30), alongside CTD salinity and temperature and the nutrient distributions.
steps.quote: were detected in SPM during spring, summer, and winter in the CRE and adjacent regions of the ECS

steps.action: Regressed DI on salinity for each season and for all seasons pooled, averaging the river stations whose salinity is near 0 (R2 = 0.82 spring, 0.94 summer, 0.65 winter, 0.72 pooled).
steps.quote: a strong correlation between DI and salinity during spring and summer

steps.action: Attributed the weaker winter correlation to southward flow of Changjiang diluted water and low discharge leaving the LCDs insufficiently mixed.
steps.quote: and the LCDs may not be sufficiently mixed.

steps.action: Kept DI as a potential salinity indicator in the CRE, especially in spring and summer.
steps.quote: the DI index showed the potential to indicate salinity changes in the CRE and the adjacent ECS regions

steps.action: Computed LDI-SST at the stations where all the required diols were detected, using the Rampen et al. (2012) calibration.
steps.quote: Our research showed that in spring, the LDI-SST ranged from 9.8 to 19.1°C

steps.action: Compared LDI-SST with in situ CTD and satellite SST: close in spring except at C2, far too cold in summer, and too warm in winter.
steps.quote: in summer, the LDI-SST ranged from 7.2°C to 22.6°C, in contrast to the measured (28.4–29.2°C) and satellite (28.8–29.7°C)

steps.action: Noted that the mismatch agrees with earlier findings of warm-season bias in LDI-SST from ECS surface sediments.
steps.quote: This result was consistent with previous studies in ECS sediments

steps.action: Proposed two explanations for the LDI-SST bias: freshwater-derived LCDs from terrestrial input, and vertical mixing or resuspension in shallow water driven by monsoon and typhoons (with Huangpu River input at C5).
steps.quote: We suggested that two main reasons for the differences between LDI-SST in SPM and observed temperatures.

steps.action: Rejected LDI-SST as a reliable SST proxy for SPM in this region.
steps.quote: we suggested the reconstructed temperature based on the LDI was not consistent with satellite-measured SST

steps.action: Ran PCA of the diols against in situ nitrate, phosphate and silicate for each season and for all seasons, and found no significant correlation between 1,14-diols and nutrients.
steps.quote: no significant correlation was found between 1,14-diols and nitrate, phosphate, or silicate concentrations

steps.action: Explained the lack of correlation by Proboscia ecology, drawing on cited studies: nutrients come from river discharge rather than upwelling, and Si/N and Si/P ratios and turbidity in the estuary disfavour Proboscia.
steps.quote: This nutrient structure may be unfavorable for the growth of Proboscia.

steps.action: Rejected 1,14-diols (NDI) as nutrient indicators in the study area.
steps.quote: Thus, 1,14-diols produced by Proboscia may not reflect nutrient conditions in the study area.

steps.action: Compiled published FC32 1,15-diol versus BIT and brGDGT data from nine river or estuary regions (Figure 7) and showed that the strength of the relation varies by region and sample type.
steps.quote: We integrated global FC32 1,15-diol index data in SPM and surface sediments

steps.action: Showed that FC32 1,15-diol decreases from river to estuary to offshore in all three seasons (71.1%, 37.4%, 16.5%) and is highest in summer.
steps.quote: Our results showed an offshore reduction of FC32 1,15-diol values (Figures 8a–8c).

steps.action: Checked FC32 1,15-diol against an independent terrestrial biomarker proxy measured on the same samples, TMBR′ in summer (R2 = 0.64).
steps.quote: The distribution of FC32 1,15-diol was also consistent with another proxy of terrestrial input, the TMBR′ index in summer

steps.action: Noted agreement with published CRE surface-sediment FC32 trends and with the FC32–BIT correlation (R2 = 0.80) reported by He et al. (2020).
steps.quote: [...] ,15-diol in surface sediments had a decreasing trend offshore in the CRE (Chen et al., 2021; He et al., 2020)

steps.action: Kept FC32 1,15-diol as a reliable proxy for riverine input to the CRE and the adjacent ECS.
steps.quote: we suggest that FC32 1,15-diol is a reliable proxy for riverine input to the CRE and adjacent regions of the ECS

steps.action: Restricted the kept proxies by season, recommending that seasonal effects be considered when applying DI and FC32 1,15-diol.
steps.quote: the effects of different seasons should be considered when using DI and FC32 1,15-diol proxies

tree.answer: Seasonal variability in how LCD proxies track salinity, SST, nutrients and riverine input in an estuary
LCDs and environmental variables measured directly in SPM and in water; proxy targets inferred through indices
Evaluate the applicability of four published proxies across three seasons
Post hoc explanations only: terrestrial input versus vertical mixing for the LDI bias; river nutrients versus upwelling for 1,14-diols
No distinct predictions derived for the rivals
Conditions found: seasons and the salinity gradient sampled on cruises

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Yes: three seasons and multiple stations along the gradient
DI weaker in winter; FC32 trend repeats across seasons and agrees with TMBR′ and sediment data
DI and FC32 kept with seasonal caveats; LDI-SST and 1,14-diols rejected for the CRE

end.claim: In CRE suspended particulate matter, DI correlates with salinity (strongly in spring and summer, R2 = 0.82 and 0.94; weaker in winter, R2 = 0.65) and FC32 1,15-diol declines from river to offshore, so both are usable salinity and riverine-input proxies, with seasonal effects to be considered.

decisive_move.sentence: The season-by-season regression of DI on salinity, together with the offshore FC32 1,15-diol gradient across seasons, is what turns the measured LCD distributions into proxy-validity claims with a stated seasonal range.

gates.evidence: Action: samples came from NSFC open cruises along an existing transect, while the seasonal SPM design was chosen to address the question (p. 2, 4). Claim: the published proxy relations could fail, and two of them did (LDI-SST mismatched in situ and satellite SST, p. 8-10; 1,14-diols showed no correlation with nutrients, p. 10). Registration: the index definitions and the Rampen LDI calibration equation were fixed in advance (p. 4); the zone boundaries, the averaging of river stations, and the explanations were chosen after the data (p. 5, 8).

imports.item: GC-MS/MS with single-ion monitoring and GC-FID with BSTFA derivatization
Principal component analysis of diols and nutrients
Proboscia diatom nutrient requirements (Si/N, Si/P ranges) used to explain 1,14-diol abundance

novelty_claims.quote: We first studied LCDs in SPM in the CRE to evaluate the seasonal variation of LCDs proxies

limits: No review file was supplied, so revisions are not visible; the acknowledgments mention an editor and two referees. Sample sizes are small: DI regressions use n = 5 (spring), 7 (summer) and 11 (winter), after the near-zero-salinity river stations are collapsed to one mean point (p. 10, Figure 5). LDI-SST could be computed only at stations where all the required diols were detected (p. 8). The explanations for the LDI bias (terrestrial input, vertical mixing) and for the 1,14-diol failure (Proboscia ecology) are not tested; they rest on cited literature (best_explanation at most, inference). The abstract singles out vertical mixing, while the discussion gives both terrestrial input and mixing. The rejection of LDI-SST and of 1,14-diols as proxies here is a sub-claim with status best_explanation (non-applicability shown by comparison; mechanism untested). NDI itself appears not to be computed: the evaluation is a PCA of 1,14-diols against nutrients (inference). TMBR′ is available for summer only. CTD and nutrient instruments differ between seasons (p. 5), and the effect of this is not assessed. The composition could also be read as independent_replication (published proxy calibrations re-checked with new data); natures_repetition was chosen because the claim is a regularity fitted across found seasonal and spatial repetitions. The supplement (Tables S1–S3) was not supplied.

disagreements.target: Gal et al. (2018) nutrient diol index / 1,14-diols as nutrient proxy
disagreements.support: PCA of SPM diols against in situ nutrients in three seasons shows no significant correlation; the authors attribute this to river-derived nutrients and a nutrient structure that disfavours Proboscia.
disagreements.quote: However, principal component analysis (PCA) was performed between LCDs in SPM and in situ measurements of nutrient concentrations

disagreements.support: LDI-SST computed from SPM departs strongly from in situ and satellite SST in summer and winter (Table 1).
disagreements.quote: LDI-SST differed from those measured in situ or by satellite

disagreements.target: Yu et al. (2018): DI may not be a reliable salinity proxy in Chinese eastern marginal seas
disagreements.support: DI–salinity regressions in SPM give R2 of 0.82 and 0.94 in spring and summer and 0.72 pooled.
disagreements.quote: the DI index showed the potential to indicate salinity changes in the CRE and the adjacent ECS regions

disagreements.target: FC32 1,15-diol as a general riverine-input proxy (de Bar et al., 2016; Lattaud, Kim, et al., 2017)
disagreements.support: A compilation of published FC32–BIT relations from nine regions shows strong, weak, or no correlation depending on region and sample type.
disagreements.quote: Therefore, the indication of FC32 1,15-diol is different in various regions and samples.

alternatives_considered.chosen: Mean salinity and mean DI of the river stations (salinity near 0) used as a single point in the regressions
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Individual river-station values, in which DI varies while salinity is about 0
alternatives_considered.reason: Salinity at the river stations is close to 0 but DI varies, consistent with earlier river studies

alternatives_considered.chosen: Both in situ CTD SST and satellite SST as references for LDI-SST
alternatives_considered.alternatives: In situ SST versus satellite SST

alternatives_considered.chosen: Both terrestrial input and vertical mixing invoked (the abstract emphasizes vertical mixing)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Freshwater-derived LCDs from terrestrial input; vertical mixing or resuspension from monsoon and typhoons
alternatives_considered.reason: Shallow nearshore stations, maximum summer runoff, and EAWM and typhoon mixing

alternatives_considered.chosen: River-derived nutrients and an unfavourable nutrient structure and turbidity for Proboscia
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Upwelling-driven nutrient supply, the basis of the NDI
alternatives_considered.reason: Changjiang discharge is the main nutrient source in the study area rather than upwelling (Han et al., 2003)
